card.problem_text:
Cook's membrane (linear elasticity, weakly symmetric mixed elements, adaptive refinement) – Lederer & Stenberg, Sec. 7.2.
Geometry: 2D tapered beam (Cook's membrane), shown in Figure 5 (left). The figure labels give the dimensions 48, 44 and 16, which match the standard Cook geometry, but the text itself does not state the vertex coordinates.
Material: Isotropic linear elasticity (not hyperelastic), E = 1, Poisson ratio ν = 0.3. Whether it is plane strain or plane stress is not stated.
Boundary conditions: Left boundary ΓD clamped. A traction is prescribed on the opposite (right) boundary. All other edges are traction-free (g = 0).
Loading: Uniform traction g = (0, 10^-3), i.e. a vertical shear load, on the right boundary opposite the clamped edge.
Discretisation in the paper: Weakly symmetric mixed finite elements (SGG2, SGG3, AFW, RAFW from Table 1) on triangulations refined adaptively by the a posteriori estimator η. RAFW was also run with uniform refinement. Element counts and mesh sizes are not stated; the only measure is the number of degrees of freedom N on the plot axes.
Features: Corner singularities of the solution. These include the corners where the clamped edge ΓD meets the traction-free top and bottom edges.; Corners where the loaded right edge meets the free edges, where the traction jumps from g to 0. This may give weaker near-singular behaviour; it is inferred from the boundary conditions..
Question: which of these quantities can serve as trustworthy reference values: A posteriori error estimator η vs N (A posteriori error estimator η plotted against the number of degrees of freedom N, for adaptive refinement (SGG2, SGG3, AFW, RAFW) and uniform refinement (RAFW). The section does not define η.); Absolute value of displacement field (|u| plotted on the adaptively refined mesh (SGG2) in Figure 5 (right).)?

spec.name: Cook's membrane: linear elasticity with weakly symmetric mixed FEM and adaptive refinement (Lederer & Stenberg, Sec. 7.2)
spec.geometry: 2D tapered quadrilateral panel (Cook's membrane), Figure 5 (left). The figure labels 48, 44 and 16 match the standard Cook geometry, with vertices assumed at (0,0), (48,44), (48,60), (0,44). The text does not give the vertex coordinates; they come from the figure labels and the standard benchmark.
spec.material: Isotropic linear elasticity, not hyperelastic: E = 1, nu = 0.3. Whether it is plane strain or plane stress is not stated. nu = 0.3 is far from incompressible, so there is no locking issue.
spec.loading: Left edge Gamma_D clamped (u = 0). Uniform traction g = (0, 1e-3), a vertical shear load, on the right edge. Top and bottom edges are traction-free (g = 0). The problem is linear and static, with no load stepping.
qois: A posteriori error estimator eta vs number of DOFs N, for adaptive refinement (SGG2, SGG3, AFW, RAFW) and uniform refinement (RAFW). eta is an error indicator, not a reference value. It can only support claims about convergence rates (adaptive runs recovering the optimal rate, uniform refinement giving a reduced, singularity-limited rate). It cannot serve as a numerical reference for any physical quantity.

Absolute displacement field |u| on the adaptively refined SGG2 mesh, Figure 5 (right). Displacement is a global/energy-type quantity that converges despite the corner singularities, but the paper shows it only as a contour plot. No point values (e.g. the usual tip deflection at (48,60)) are reported, so it can only be checked qualitatively, not used as a quantitative reference.
well_posedness: Dirichlet condition on the whole left edge Gamma_D removes all rigid-body modes, so the linear elasticity problem has a unique solution (Korn inequality, E > 0, -1 < nu < 0.5).
Material is stable: nu = 0.3 with E = 1 gives a positive definite elasticity tensor, and it is far from the incompressible limit, so the mixed methods need no special robustness here.
The problem is linear, so there are no limit points, buckling or load-level effects. The small traction 1e-3 only scales the solution.

Singular feature: at the corners where the clamped left edge meets the traction-free top and bottom edges, stresses are singular (u is in H^{1+s} with s < 1). Pointwise peak stress, and stress near these corners, will not converge under refinement and cannot be a reference value.

Near-singular feature: at the corners where the loaded right edge meets the free edges, the traction jumps from g to 0. This likely causes weaker singular behaviour; it is inferred from the boundary conditions and not stated in the paper.

Because of the singularities, uniform refinement gives a reduced convergence rate in eta/energy. Adaptive refinement can recover optimal rates. Energy norm, displacements and region-averaged stresses do converge.
The domain shape (a convex quadrilateral with no re-entrant corner) is not the source of the singularity; the mixed boundary conditions are.
open_questions: Plane strain or plane stress? The paper does not say, and the effective moduli and displacement values depend on it.
Exact vertex coordinates: only the figure labels 48/44/16 are given. Confirm the standard Cook geometry (0,0),(48,44),(48,60),(0,44).
Definition of the a posteriori estimator eta: it is not defined in Sec. 7.2. Is it a reliable and efficient upper bound for the stress/energy error, and with what constants?

Element enum: SGG2, SGG3, AFW and RAFW are weakly symmetric mixed stress-displacement-rotation elements on triangles. None of them is in the allowed enum; T6 is only a proxy for 'triangular, higher order'. Polynomial degrees and DOF definitions should come from Table 1.
Element counts, mesh sizes, the marking strategy (e.g. Dorfler parameter) and the initial mesh are not given; N on the plot axes is the only measure.

No numerical value of any QoI is reported (no tip displacement, no energy), so there is no quantitative reference value. Can tip vertical displacement or strain energy be extracted from the source, or would it have to be recomputed and checked against published Cook-membrane linear-elastic values?
What corner singularity exponents (Williams-type, clamped-free and loaded-free corners at the given angles, nu = 0.3) does one expect to compare against the uniform-refinement rate of eta?

assumptions: The traction value 0.001 is the decimal form of the stated 10^-3 in 'g = (0, 10^-3)'; it is not a new number.
Plane strain is assumed because the text does not say whether the problem is plane strain or plane stress. This changes the displacement magnitudes, so the choice should be confirmed.
The geometry is the standard Cook's membrane, outer [[0,0],[48,44],[48,60],[0,44]], under rule (4). The text names the benchmark and the figure labels 48, 44 and 16 match it.
The traction g is taken as a constant force per unit length on the right edge x = 48, in the global y direction.

The top-right corner (48,60) is used as a displacement point of interest. The paper gives no reference value there: Figure 5 (right) shows only a contour plot of |u|. The estimator η has no pipeline equivalent, and the section does not define it.
